$comment: Generated by scripts/prove-guards.mjs. Each result is the outcome of running the guard twice in a sandbox: once on a clean baseline, once after a declared violation. The fixtures live in data/guards.json.

results.reason: Drives five real pages with Playwright role/label locators against a running server, including a signed-in session for avatar-limited steps. A static fixture cannot prove an accessibility-tree locator resolves against live markup.
Drives a real browser over the live page set and reads the console, so it needs Playwright and a running server. A static fixture cannot produce a runtime console error.

The run stage boots the real server on a free port and probes every cron URL, so the check is inherently live. The probe is deliberately unauthenticated and every handler fails closed on CRON_SECRET, so no job body executes: nothing is paid, swapped, minted, transferred, or written. `--static` skips the boot for a route-and-load-only pass.

Needs Playwright plus a server serving dist/, because the thing under test is the browser's own policy evaluation against a real response. A static fixture cannot produce a securitypolicyviolation event.

It reads the production wallet table and the live encryption key, then decrypts in memory to test each secret against the current key. There is no offline fixture for 'this ciphertext no longer opens' that would prove anything about the real fleet. Read-only: it never writes, signs, or broadcasts.

results.reason: It reads the production home_connections table and the live encryption key, then decrypts in memory to test each token against the current key. There is no offline fixture for "this ciphertext no longer opens" that would prove anything about the real fleet. Read-only: it never writes and never opens a socket to any house.

Serves pages/ibm/ from a throwaway origin and lets it talk to a real three.ws over the network, because the thing under test is the browser enforcing cross-origin rules against live response headers. Any stub or proxy would answer for three.ws and satisfy CORS on the browser behalf, blinding the audit to the only failure it exists to catch.
